judged_text: `minimumTokenResponseSchema`'s computed keys (`[z.string().toString()]`) evaluate to the static string "[object Object]" and don't create index signatures, so the effective schema is `{ access_token: string }` and everything else (e.g. `expiry_date`/`expires_in`) is stripped — refreshed credentials keep a stale or missing expiry, causing re-refresh on every call or failure once the access token TTL lapses

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In a JS object literal, those computed property expressions are evaluated immediately to strings; with Zod, `z.string().toString()` is not an index signature and will resolve to a single static key (likely `"[object Object]"`). As a result, the schema effectively only defines `access_token` (plus at most one bogus literal property) and, since Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in` would be stripped when this minimum schema is used. That aligns with the reported consequence: refreshed credentials can lose expiry information, causing repeated refresh attempts or failures when tokens expire.
